doc.dbt.__overview__.block_contents:
### Welcome!

Welcome to the auto-generated documentation for your dbt project!

### Navigation

You can use the `Project` and `Database` navigation tabs on the left side of the window to explore the models
in your project.

#### Project Tab
The `Project` tab mirrors the directory structure of your dbt project. In this tab, you can see all of the
models defined in your dbt project, as well as models imported from dbt packages.

#### Database Tab
The `Database` tab also exposes your models, but in a format that looks more like a database explorer. This view
shows relations (tables and views) grouped into database schemas. Note that ephemeral models are _not_ shown
in this interface, as they do not exist in the database.

### Graph Exploration
You can click the blue icon on the bottom-right corner of the page to view the lineage graph of your models.

On model pages, you'll see the immediate parents and children of the model you're exploring. By clicking the `Expand`
button at the top-right of this lineage pane, you'll be able to see all of the models that are used to build,
or are built from, the model you're exploring.

Once expanded, you'll be able to use the `--select` and `--exclude` model selection syntax to filter the
models in the graph. For more information on model selection, check out the [dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/model-selection-syntax).

Note that you can also right-click on models to interactively filter and explore the graph.

---

### More information

- [What is dbt](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/introduction)?
- Read the [dbt viewpoint](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/viewpoint)
- [Installation](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/installation)
- Join the [dbt Community](https://www.getdbt.com/community/) for questions and discussion

exposure.whyline_denver_dbt.whyline_denv.name: whyline_denver_app
exposure.whyline_denver_dbt.whyline_denv.description:
Next.js dashboard backed by FastAPI, querying curated marts through DuckDB or BigQuery.
The reliability marts count observed stop visits (core.fct_stop_visit) since the
stop-visit cutover; earlier partitions keep the legacy sampled method.

model.whyline_denver_dbt.stg_rt_events.name: stg_rt_events
model.whyline_denver_dbt.stg_rt_events.description: LEGACY (disabled at the stop-visit cutover): one sampled trip-update and vehicle-position row per feed poll x trip. Replaced by the stream views and core.fct_stop_visit.
model.whyline_denver_dbt.stg_rt_events.raw_code:
{{
    config(
        enabled=false,
        materialized='incremental',
        unique_key=['feed_ts_utc', 'trip_id'],
        partition_by={'field': 'event_date_mst', 'data_type': 'date'},
        cluster_by=['route_id', 'trip_id'],
        incremental_strategy='merge',
        incremental_predicates=["DBT_INTERNAL_DEST.event_date_mst >= date_sub(current_date('America/Denver'), interval 3 day)"]
    )
}}

{#
LEGACY, frozen at the stop-visit cutover (enabled=false keeps the table but stops all runs and
tests). It sampled one predicted terminal arrival per poll and trip, not observed stop arrivals;
fct_stop_visit replaces it. Remove the flag only to rebuild history deliberately.
Silver: trip updates merged with vehicle positions, one row per feed poll x trip. Reported
delays only; schedule-derived delays and dimension keys are added in core.fct_trip_observation.
- Full refresh: 45-day lookback (raise rt_events_lookback_days to rebuild from all bronze)
- Incremental: last 12 hours of feeds
#}
{% set lookback_days = var('rt_events_lookback_days', 45) %}
{% set incremental_hours = var('rt_events_incremental_hours', 12) %}

with tu as (
    select
        feed_ts_utc,
        entity_id as tu_entity_id,
        trip_id,
        route_id,
        stop_id,
        stop_sequence,
        arrival_delay_sec as arrival_delay_sec_raw,
        departure_delay_sec as departure_delay_sec_raw,
        schedule_relationship,
        event_ts_utc as tu_event_ts_utc
    from {{ source('raw','raw_gtfsrt_trip_updates') }}
    where feed_ts_utc >= timestamp_sub(current_timestamp(), interval {% if is_incremental() %}{{ incremental_hours }} hour{% else %}{{ lookback_days }} day{% endif %})
      and date(feed_ts_utc) >= date_sub(current_date(), interval {% if is_incremental() %}1{% else %}{{ lookback_days }}{% endif %} day)  -- Explicit partition filter
),
vp as (
    select
        feed_ts_utc,
        entity_id as vp_entity_id,
        trip_id,
        route_id,
        vehicle_id,
        vehicle_label,
        lon,
        lat,
        bearing,
        speed_mps,
        event_ts_utc as vp_event_ts_utc
    from {{ source('raw','raw_gtfsrt_vehicle_positions') }}
    where feed_ts_utc >= timestamp_sub(current_timestamp(), interval {% if is_incremental() %}{{ incremental_hours }} hour{% else %}{{ lookback_days }} day{% endif %})
      and date(feed_ts_utc) >= date_sub(current_date(), interval {% if is_incremental() %}1{% else %}{{ lookback_days }}{% endif %} day)  -- Explicit partition filter
),
j as (
    select
        coalesce(tu.feed_ts_utc, vp.feed_ts_utc) as feed_ts_utc,
        coalesce(tu.trip_id, vp.trip_id) as trip_id,
        coalesce(tu.route_id, vp.route_id) as route_id,
        tu.tu_entity_id,
        vp.vp_entity_id,
        tu.stop_id,
        tu.stop_sequence,
        tu.arrival_delay_sec_raw,
        tu.departure_delay_sec_raw,
        tu.schedule_relationship,
        vp.vehicle_id,
        vp.vehicle_label,
        vp.lon,
        vp.lat,
        vp.bearing,
        vp.speed_mps,
        {{ make_point('vp.lon','vp.lat') }} as geom,
        coalesce(tu.tu_event_ts_utc, vp.vp_event_ts_utc, coalesce(tu.feed_ts_utc, vp.feed_ts_utc)) as event_ts_utc
    from tu
    full outer join vp
        on tu.feed_ts_utc = vp.feed_ts_utc
        and tu.trip_id = vp.trip_id
        and tu.route_id = vp.route_id
    -- A NULL trip_id never matches the MERGE key, so these rows were re-inserted every run
    where coalesce(tu.trip_id, vp.trip_id) is not null
),
ranked as (
    select
        *,
        row_number() over (
            partition by feed_ts_utc, trip_id
            order by event_ts_utc desc, tu_entity_id desc, vp_entity_id desc
        ) as trip_rank
    from j
)
select
    r.feed_ts_utc,
    r.trip_id,
    r.route_id,
    r.tu_entity_id,
    r.vp_entity_id,
    r.stop_id,
    r.stop_sequence,
    r.arrival_delay_sec_raw as arrival_delay_sec,
    r.departure_delay_sec_raw as departure_delay_sec,
    r.schedule_relationship,
    r.vehicle_id,
    r.vehicle_label,
    r.lon,
    r.lat,
    r.bearing,
    r.speed_mps,
    r.geom,
    r.event_ts_utc,
    {{ date_mst('r.event_ts_utc') }} as event_date_mst,
    {{ hour_mst('r.event_ts_utc') }} as event_hour_mst
from ranked as r
where r.trip_rank = 1

model.whyline_denver_dbt.fct_trip_observ.name: fct_trip_observation
model.whyline_denver_dbt.fct_trip_observ.description: LEGACY (disabled at the stop-visit cutover): one sampled prediction per feed poll x trip, usually of the trip's terminal arrival, not an observed stop arrival. delay_sec defaulted unknown delays to 0. Replaced by fct_stop_visit.
model.whyline_denver_dbt.fct_trip_observ.raw_code:
{{
    config(
        enabled=false,
        materialized='incremental',
        incremental_strategy='merge',
        unique_key=['feed_ts_utc', 'trip_id'],
        partition_by={'field': 'service_date_mst', 'data_type': 'date'},
        cluster_by=['route_id', 'stop_id'],
        incremental_predicates=["DBT_INTERNAL_DEST.service_date_mst >= date_sub(current_date('America/Denver'), interval 3 day)"]
    )
}}

{#
LEGACY, frozen at the stop-visit cutover (enabled=false keeps the table but stops all runs and
tests). It sampled one predicted terminal arrival per poll and trip, not observed stop arrivals;
fct_stop_visit replaces it. Remove the flag only to rebuild history deliberately.
Grain: one realtime observation per feed poll x trip (sampled, not every arrival).
Delay resolution: the reported delay, else event time minus the scheduled time for the
same trip/stop/date, else NULL in *_raw and 0 in delay_sec (counted as on time).
Natural keys are carried next to the surrogate keys so the 15-minute marts avoid dim joins.
#}

with obs as (
    select
        feed_ts_utc,
        trip_id,
        route_id,
        stop_id,
        stop_sequence,
        event_ts_utc,
        event_date_mst,
        event_hour_mst,
        arrival_delay_sec,
        departure_delay_sec,
        schedule_relationship,
        vehicle_id,
        vehicle_label,
        lat,
        lon,
        bearing,
        speed_mps
    from {{ ref('stg_rt_events') }}
    {% if is_incremental() %}
    where event_date_mst >= date_sub(current_date('America/Denver'), interval 3 day)
      and feed_ts_utc >= timestamp_sub(current_timestamp(), interval {{ var('rt_events_incremental_hours', 12) }} hour)
    {% endif %}
),
sched as (
    select
        trip_id,
        stop_id,
        stop_sequence,
        service_date_mst,
        sched_arrival_ts_mst,
        sched_departure_ts_mst
    from {{ ref('fct_scheduled_stop_time') }}
    {% if is_incremental() %}
    -- Constant bounds so BigQuery prunes; the schedule extends ~30 days ahead
    where service_date_mst between date_sub(current_date('America/Denver'), interval 3 day)
        and date_add(current_date('America/Denver'), interval 1 day)
    {% endif %}
),
resolved as (
    select
        o.*,
        coalesce(
            o.arrival_delay_sec,
            timestamp_diff(o.event_ts_utc, s.sched_arrival_ts_mst, second)
        ) as arrival_delay_resolved_sec,
        coalesce(
            o.departure_delay_sec,
            timestamp_diff(o.event_ts_utc, s.sched_departure_ts_mst, second)
        ) as departure_delay_resolved_sec
    from obs as o
    left join sched as s
        on o.trip_id = s.trip_id
        and o.stop_id = s.stop_id
        and o.stop_sequence = s.stop_sequence
        and o.event_date_mst = s.service_date_mst
)

select
    r.feed_ts_utc,
    r.trip_id,
    r.route_id,
    r.stop_id,
    r.stop_sequence,
    r.event_date_mst as service_date_mst,
    r.event_hour_mst,
    r.event_ts_utc,
    coalesce(dt.trip_key, -1) as trip_key,
    coalesce(dr.route_key, -1) as route_key,
    coalesce(ds.stop_key, -1) as stop_key,
    dt.direction_id,
    r.arrival_delay_sec as arrival_delay_reported_sec,
    r.departure_delay_sec as departure_delay_reported_sec,
    r.arrival_delay_sec is not null or r.departure_delay_sec is not null as is_delay_reported,
    coalesce(r.arrival_delay_resolved_sec, r.departure_delay_resolved_sec) as delay_sec_raw,
    coalesce(r.arrival_delay_resolved_sec, r.departure_delay_resolved_sec, 0) as delay_sec,
    r.schedule_relationship,
    r.vehicle_id,
    r.vehicle_label,
    r.lat,
    r.lon,
    r.bearing,
    r.speed_mps
from resolved as r
left join {{ ref('dim_trip') }} as dt
    on dt.trip_id = r.trip_id
    and r.event_date_mst between dt.valid_from and dt.valid_to
left join {{ ref('dim_route') }} as dr
    on dr.route_id = r.route_id
    and r.event_date_mst between dr.valid_from and dr.valid_to
left join {{ ref('dim_stop') }} as ds
    on ds.stop_id = r.stop_id
    and r.event_date_mst between ds.valid_from and ds.valid_to

model.whyline_denver_dbt.fct_stop_arriva.name: fct_stop_arrival
model.whyline_denver_dbt.fct_stop_arriva.description: LEGACY (disabled at the stop-visit cutover): headways between sampled predicted terminal arrivals, not observed stop arrivals. Replaced by headways between consecutive fct_stop_visit rows in mart_reliability_by_stop_hour.
model.whyline_denver_dbt.fct_stop_arriva.raw_code:
{{
    config(
        enabled=false,
        materialized='incremental',
        incremental_strategy='merge',
        unique_key='stop_arrival_key',
        partition_by={'field': 'service_date_mst', 'data_type': 'date'},
        cluster_by=['route_id', 'stop_id'],
        incremental_predicates=["DBT_INTERNAL_DEST.service_date_mst >= date_sub(current_date('America/Denver'), interval 4 day)"]
    )
}}

{#
LEGACY, frozen at the stop-visit cutover (enabled=false keeps the table but stops all runs and
tests). It sampled one predicted terminal arrival per poll and trip, not observed stop arrivals;
fct_stop_visit replaces it. Remove the flag only to rebuild history deliberately.
Grain: one observed stop event per route x direction x stop x service date x event time,
with the observed headway, the nearest scheduled headway, and an adherence flag.
Incremental: 3 days; full refresh: rt_events_lookback_days.
#}
{% set window_days = 3 if is_incremental() else var('rt_events_lookback_days', 45) %}

with obs_events as (
    select
        route_id,
        direction_id,
        stop_id,
        service_date_mst,
        event_ts_utc,
        any_value(route_key) as route_key,
        any_value(stop_key) as stop_key
    from {{ ref('fct_trip_observation') }}
    where event_ts_utc is not null
      and service_date_mst >= date_sub(current_date('America/Denver'), interval {{ window_days }} day)
    group by route_id, direction_id, stop_id, service_date_mst, event_ts_utc
),
obs as (
    select
        *,
        timestamp_diff(
            event_ts_utc,
            lag(event_ts_utc) over (
                partition by route_id, direction_id, stop_id, service_date_mst
                order by event_ts_utc
            ),
            second
        ) as obs_headway_sec
    from obs_events
),
sched_events as (
    select distinct
        route_id,
        direction_id,
        stop_id,
        service_date_mst,
        sched_arrival_ts_mst
    from {{ ref('fct_scheduled_stop_time') }}
    where sched_arrival_ts_mst is not null
      -- Constant bounds so BigQuery prunes; the schedule extends ~30 days ahead
      and service_date_mst between date_sub(current_date('America/Denver'), interval {{ window_days }} day)
        and date_add(current_date('America/Denver'), interval 1 day)
),
sch as (
    select
        *,
        timestamp_diff(
            sched_arrival_ts_mst,
            lag(sched_arrival_ts_mst) over (
                partition by route_id, direction_id, stop_id, service_date_mst
                order by sched_arrival_ts_mst
            ),
            second
        ) as sch_headway_sec
    from sched_events
),
nearest as (
    select
        o.route_id,
        o.direction_id,
        o.stop_id,
        o.service_date_mst,
        o.event_ts_utc,
        o.route_key,
        o.stop_key,
        o.obs_headway_sec,
        s.sch_headway_sec,
        abs(timestamp_diff(o.event_ts_utc, s.sched_arrival_ts_mst, second)) as dt_abs
    from obs as o
    join sch as s
        on o.route_id = s.route_id
        and coalesce(o.direction_id, -1) = coalesce(s.direction_id, -1)
        and o.stop_id = s.stop_id
        and o.service_date_mst = s.service_date_mst
    where o.obs_headway_sec is not null
      and s.sch_headway_sec is not null
    qualify row_number() over (
        partition by o.route_id, o.direction_id, o.stop_id, o.service_date_mst, o.event_ts_utc
        order by dt_abs
    ) = 1
)

select
    farm_fingerprint(concat(
        route_id, '|', coalesce(cast(direction_id as string), ''), '|', stop_id, '|',
        cast(service_date_mst as string), '|', cast(event_ts_utc as string)
    )) as stop_arrival_key,
    route_id,
    direction_id,
    stop_id,
    service_date_mst,
    event_ts_utc,
    route_key,
    stop_key,
    obs_headway_sec,
    sch_headway_sec,
    dt_abs,
    case
        when dt_abs <= {{ var('sched_match_tol_sec', 1800) }}
         and sch_headway_sec > 0
         and abs(obs_headway_sec - sch_headway_sec) / sch_headway_sec <= {{ var('headway_tol_ratio', 0.5) }}
        then 1
        else 0
    end as headway_adherent
from nearest
